text:
Anaheim comes to Edmonton two days after a 5-4 win at Vancouver, where Cutter Gauthier scored three goals, and sits at 3-1-1 in its last five. The Oilers are 3-0-2 but had a three-game winning streak end in a 4-3 shootout loss at New Jersey. Both teams are missing forwards: Zach Hyman (neck) for EDM, with Colton Dach moving up beside Kapanen and Nugent-Hopkins, and A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling for ANA. It's also a rematch of last spring's first-round series, which the Ducks won in six, though EDM took the Oct 7 meeting 5-2.

Our numbers lean Edmonton, 3.24 expected goals to 2.90 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). At five on five the Ducks have taken 44% of those chances to the Oilers' 49%, and Anaheim allows 3.48 per 60 minutes. Edmonton's power play, at 0.88 expected goals a game, meets a Ducks penalty kill allowing 0.82, and ANA takes 5.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Lukas Dostal (+0.26 goals saved above expected, a measure of how many goals a goalie stops beyond what his shots suggest) and Matt Tomkins (+1.44 in one game) face off. Dostal was at -3.71 over 56 games last season.

Gauthier, at 40% to score, is the Ducks' main threat, and Leo Carlsson is 73% for a point. For Edmonton, Leon Draisaitl is 46% to score and Connor McDavid, on a 16-game point streak, is 93% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks are Kasperi Kapanen, 46% for a point after his bump in minutes, and fourth-liner Filip Hallander, at 12% to score on dangerous recent shots. Both are players to watch, not locks.
